layers.message: Add analyst guide for exporting records
Start documentation cycle for export guide
Record project context for export guide

graderOnly: docs/guide/exporting.md already documents every option, default, output form, quoting rule, empty-input behavior, and error message (with exit status) that src/cli.js and src/csv.js implement; no statement in it is inaccurate, so no documentation edit is needed to satisfy the request.

Active Work.Request holds the explicit standalone Documenter assignment (target FILE docs/guide/exporting.md, AUTONOMOUS, user style NONE) that the previous commit had saved in PendingCycleRequest while a pending STANDARD preference blocked cycle creation.

A correct scope states accuracy and coverage outcomes for the guide that an assessed no-change result can satisfy, keeps behavior changes out of scope, and hands off to Architect; the documentation route still requires Architect, Documenter, final Reviewer, and Synchronizer.

all.why: a correct run persists the first scope for the cycle at the artifact init path

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 00-project (pre-install): a dependency-free Node ESM CLI, bin/export.js plus src/cli.js and src/csv.js, sample data, and node:test tests. 05-guide (pre-install): docs/guide/exporting.md, an accurate analyst guide covering options, defaults, examples with real output, quoting, empty input, and every error message and exit status; README links it. 50-pending-request: STATE.md with Active Work UNSET and a blocked standalone Documenter request in PendingCycleRequest (pending STANDARD preference conflict) so the formerly-pending fact is true in history. 51-start-cycle: STATE.md starts the DOCUMENTATION cycle guide-20261004T120000Z-1a2b3c4d at AUDITING (INITIAL, policy NONE) with the request moved to Active Work.Request and pending fields cleared. 52-context: Auditor-owned .standards/CONTEXT.md recording the command behavior and that the guide matches it, and STATE.md at SCOPING with FORWARD from AUDITING, Scope/Architecture/Development NONE. The spec sets date so the cycle ID timestamp is not after the commit dates. Layer code avoids template literals so no dollar-brace text appears in layer files.
